Based on current Belgian/Brussels-Capital Region legislation, here is a full breakdown of your situation:

## 1. Is it mandatory, and are there exemptions?

Yes.

content.text: This parcours d'intégration is mandatory - subject to exemption - for first-time arrivals aged 18 to 65 of foreign nationality, legally resident for less than three years and holding a residence permit valid for more than three months.

Your profile (40 years old, non-EU, residence permit >3 months, legally resident <3 years, first registration in a Brussels commune) places you squarely in the mandatory target group.

More precisely, the Flemish-side guidance specifies the cumulative conditions:

citations.title: Wie is verplicht tot inburgering in Brussel?

content.text: you must be a foreigner (non-EU+ nationality), between 18 and 65 years old when the obligation arises, and registered for the first time in the foreigners' register of one of the 19 Brussels communes with a residence permit valid for more than three months, after 1 June 2022

(the date the obligation entered into force).

**Exemptions** include:
-

citations.cited_text: Le primo-arrivant peut bénéficier d’une exemption s’il vient d’un pays de l’Union Européenne ou s’il a déjà obtenu une attestation d’intégration.
citations.title: Du neuf pour le Parcours d’accueil des primo-arrivants à Bruxelles ...

content.text: Exemption if you come from an EU country or if you have already obtained an integration attestation.
- Also exempt if you already hold a diploma from a school organized/funded by the Flemish, French, or German-speaking Community

citations.title: Wie is verplicht tot inburgering in Brussel?

content.text: (diploma or certificate of basic, secondary or higher education obtained in an institution financed, organized or subsidized by the Flemish Community, French Community or German-speaking Community)

.

If a person required to follow the programme fails to complete it,
